ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed general partners, limited partners exercising significant control, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must undergo mandatory screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, Canada's Listed Entities under the Criminal Code, and Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act. Screening must be completed within 90 days prior to filing, documented in the AML/CFT file, and refreshed prior to any disbursement or capital injection, in accordance with FINTRAC compliance program requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (Corporations Online / BC Registry Services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed limited partnership name must be in English or French, expressed in roman characters, and must not contain special characters other than approved punctuation, accents, and symbols acceptable to the British Columbia Registrar of Companies. All names must be distinguishable from existing names and may be subject to limited consequential use and misdescriptive word review under the BC Business Corporations Act naming rules applicable to the BC Partnership Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation cannot be extended. If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a new name reservation request online through BC Corporate Online. A formal administrative reconsideration may be filed with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of rejection, including supporting legal arguments and evidence of distinguishability; a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of British Columbia by way of judicial review. All appeal submissions must be accompanied by the original name rejection notice and the reserved-name search report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The British Columbia Partnership Act requires the limited partnership to maintain a registered office and records office at a physical street address in British Columbia. Virtual office services are permissible only if they include a physical street address in BC for service of process and access to statutory records; pure virtual services without a physical location are not compliant. For digital webtoon publishing, a virtual office with a physical street address and document-access capabilities is generally acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5/100 (low-moderate); such inspections are risk-based, with increased probability if the entity relies on nominee principals, concentrated non-resident control, or non-arms-length cross-border transactions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, ss. 7-9 (registration and certificate) and s. 20 (registered office); Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348 (general partnership rules incorporated by reference)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) filed under the Limited Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, s. 7
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital contribution is imposed on limited partnerships under British Columbia law; capital is fixed by the partnership agreement and may be cash or property; no government-mandated escrow account exists, but the General Partner resolution elects a segregated escrow bank account to hold contributed capital pending completion of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The sole General Partner subscribes to the initial capital contribution specified in the Partnership Agreement, which shall be deposited into an escrow account at a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank; 2. The registered office in British Columbia shall be situated at the address recorded in the Declaration of Limited Partnership, and the records keeper shall maintain the partnership register, books, and records at that office; 3. The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until removed by the General Partner; 4. The officers are authorized to execute all banking, regulatory, and commercial documents necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services via the OneStop Business Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request through the BC Corporate Online platform, selecting a name that ends with 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.'; the system performs a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) against both federal and provincial records; pay the name reservation fee and obtain an approved name reservation certificate valid for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt for name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused due to conflict or confusion with an existing trademark or corporate name, submit a revised name request within the validity period, or apply for a minor amendment to the reservation; any dispute of the registrar's refusal may be appealed in writing to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form LP-1 providing the registered name, registered office address in British Columbia, full names and addresses of the general partner and of the initial limited partners, the aggregate amount of capital contributed by each limited partner, and the appointment of the records keeper; execute the declaration by the general partner; if the general partner is a non-resident, have the signature notarized or certified in accordance with BC Evidence Act requirements.
required_dossiers: Executed Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1)
Consent to act as records keeper
Consent to use property as registered office
Certified copy of the general partner's certificate of good standing (if corporate general partner)
Notarized Power of Attorney for foreign officers (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry examiner issues a requisition, correct the stated deficiencies (e.g., incomplete Schedule, missing consent, defect in name) and re-submit the amended declaration online; an appeal of the requisition may be lodged with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the date of requisition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration and Obtain Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online filing system (BC Registries)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed PDF of Form LP-1 to BC Corporate Online, pay the statutory filing fee of CAD 40 via approved payment gateway, and transmit the filing; upon acceptance, BC Registries issues the Certificate of Registration under section 8 of the Limited Partnership Act, which establishes the limited partnership's legal existence.
required_dossiers: Approved Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for illegibility, missing pages, or fee errors, correct the document and immediately re-file; if the certificate is not issued within the service standard, contact the BC Registries contact centre for expedited manual review; there is no statutory right of appeal for a rejected filing, but a new filing may be submitted without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC Ministry of Finance; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) and CRA program accounts for GST/HST and employee payroll; register the limited partnership with WorkSafeBC for workers' compensation coverage; register with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST if the partnership will sell taxable digital goods or services in the province; open a corporate bank account previously designated in the escrow resolution.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the business number application due to partnership identity verification, provide the Certificate of Registration and proof of the general partner's identity; if WorkSafeBC proposes an incorrect industry classification code, file a request for reclassification with the WorkSafeBC Classification Committee within the statutory appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Maintenance and Annual Compliance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain a registered office in British Columbia at the address stated in the Declaration; appoint a records keeper to hold the partnership register, books, and records; annually file the limited partnership annual report with BC Registries, update any changes to the general partner, limited partners, or registered office via the applicable amendment forms, and pay the annual filing fee.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as records keeper (on change)
Amendment of Declaration forms (Form LP-2 or equivalent) (if changes occur)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual report is filed late, a late filing penalty is assessed and the limited partnership may be struck from the register; remedy by filing the overdue annual report online, paying the penalty, and, if dissolved administratively, applying for restoration under the Business Corporations Act restoration procedure or re-filing a Declaration of Limited Partnership.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the business activity of digital webtoon publishing (NAICS 511130) is classified as an information and cultural industry, not manufacturing, and is not subject to any industrial licensing board in British Columbia; if physical office premises are occupied, the applicable authority is the municipal licensing and building department of the city in which the office is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for digital webtoon publishing and multilanguage chapter unlocking; however, if the partnership maintains a physical office it must obtain a Municipal Business Licence, an Occupancy Permit under the local zoning bylaw, and be registered with WorkSafeBC as an employer.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Environmental Assessment Office, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based digital publishing is not a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 43; no environmental assessment certificate or registration filing is required for the described activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharges or stationary-source VOC emissions are generated by webtoon publishing and syndication; compliance is required with the BC Recycling Regulation (B.C. Reg. 449/2004) for disposal of e-waste and electronic media, municipal solid waste and recycling bylaws, and, where applicable, the BC Energy Step Code for office building energy efficiency; office data centers and servers, if owned, must meet the electrical efficiency requirements of the BC Clean Energy Act and municipal noise bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The partnership must obtain a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate in accordance with the British Columbia Fire Code (B.C. Reg. 213/2006) for any leased or owned office premises; all workplaces must pass structural load verification and occupancy classification under the Vancouver Building Bylaw or applicable municipal building code, including egress routes, wheelchair accessibility, and life-safety systems; the partnership must obtain a WorkSafeBC occupation health and safety clearance certificate prior to hiring employees and must post the certificate at the workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account administered through CRA 'My Business Account' at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html and Business Registration Online (BRO). British Columbia Minister of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch administers PST via the eTaxBC portal at https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/sales-taxes/pst; PST tax number is separate from the federal BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Apply to CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) using the BRO online service or Form RC1 ('Request for a Business Number'). Step 2: Register the Limited Partnership for GST/HST under the same BN once worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (ETA s.148(1)); registration is effective on the day the threshold is exceeded and is compulsory in the following calendar month. Step 3: If the LP is a non-resident supplier of digital services (not the present fact pattern, as the LP is Canadian), use CRA's simplified non-resident GST/HST registration channel with no Canadian permanent establishment requirement. Step 4: For BC PST, register separately with the BC Ministry of Finance before making BC-source taxable sales; foreign sellers must register once gross BC taxable sales exceed CAD 10,000 in a calendar year. Step 5: File annual partnership information return (T5013) naming all partners with their residency, CRA BN (if any) and share of income; non-resident partners must provide foreign tax identification numbers and may face Part XIII withholding on certain payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. A BC Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent for federal income tax under ITA s.96(1); the LP itself pays no Part I income tax, and each partner is taxed on its allocable share of partnership income. For GST/HST purposes, the partnership is a distinct 'person' under ETA s.272.1 and must account for GST/HST in its own capacity, with partners jointly and severally liable for the LP's unremitted GST/HST under ETA s.273. Territorial scope: Canadian-resident partners taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners taxed only on Canadian-source income (ITA s.2(3)/115), with the LP potentially classified as a 'non-Canadian partnership' under ITA s.102 if any partner is a non-resident. No tax-exempt zone or preferential regime applies to this entity in British Columbia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows the mandatory flow-through rules of ITA ss.96-103. Available elections relevant to a cross-border webtoon LP: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s.240(3) before crossing the CAD 30,000 threshold, enabling input tax credit recovery on Canadian expenses; (ii) election to use the GST/HST 'net tax' simplified accounting? Not applicable to Large/medium; the standard net tax method applies automatically. A partnership may elect under ETA s.273(1) to treat a partner as acting as agent for collection only in limited circumstances. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss.18.4(3), 95, 247(2) and ETA s.12.6 are mandatory and cannot be elected out; however, a taxpayer may file a contemporaneous documentation election to self-identify mismatch treatment for penalty relief under the CRA's disclosure rules. No statutory check-the-box or 'hybrid entity classification' election exists in Canada.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual federal-provincial system: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added tax at 5%, plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST), a separate retail sales tax at 7%. Digital webtoon subscriptions and in-app comic unlocking are subject to GST on supplies to Canadian-recipient consumers; BC PST currently does not apply to intangible digital content downloaded or streamed electronically (PST applies only to enumerated tangible goods and taxable services). Platform-mediated sales via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are subject to GST if the end consumer is in Canada; the non-resident platform typically collects and remits GST on the consumer-facing sale, while the LP's royalty sale to the platform is generally zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 for GST/HST small-supplier registration (worldwide taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or in the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters; ETA s.148(1)). Non-resident digital suppliers cross the same CAD 30,000 threshold for simplified GST/HST registration. For BC PST: foreign sellers with BC taxable sales exceeding CAD 10,000 in a calendar year must register as PST collectors; Canadian sellers with a BC establishment must register before making their first taxable sale regardless of revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None federally. Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government API pre-authorization of invoices, and no digital stamping for GST/HST. The CRA accepts standard paper and electronic invoices; each invoice must show the supplier's name and BN, date, description, consideration, and GST/HST charged or zero-rating indication. A voluntary PEPPOL-based 'Canada e-invoicing' framework exists and is CRA-compatible. Quebec's B2B e-invoicing mandate (2025-2026) does not extend to British Columbia. BC PST requires only standard invoices and periodic eTaxBC filing; no pre-clearance or stamping obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of intangible personal property (digital webtoon content licenses, subscriptions, and chapter-unlocking rights) made to a recipient who is a non-resident and not registered for GST/HST are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.25, where the supply is delivered or made available outside Canada. Digital services supplied to a non-resident are likewise zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s.23, provided no supply of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada is involved. Eligibility is established by: (i) non-resident status of the counterparty (Apple/Google platform entities are typically resident in Ireland or the US; obtain W-8BEN-E or a Certificate of Residence); (ii) electronic delivery logs and IP geolocation showing downloads/access outside Canada; (iii) contract language expressing foreign distribution rights; (iv) foreign-currency proceeds from foreign payors; and (v) absence of any tangible medium crossing a Canadian customs border. Where Apple IAP or Google Play Billing is used, the LP's supply of distribution rights to the non-resident platform is zero-rated, and the platform may separately collect GST/HST from Canadian consumers under the digital platform rules. If any end-user access is traced to Canada, the consideration allocable to that access is subject to 5% GST and must be self-assessed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A) - mandatory only where physical media containing webtoon content is shipped internationally; for pure electronic delivery, an internal digital-export log with timestamps, file delivery server addresses, and IP geolocation report substitutes.

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill - mandatory only for physical shipments of comic/graphic novel media; for digital webtoon syndication, the contractual delivery certificate and platform download server logs are retained in lieu.

Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Bank Records (SWIFT MT103, bank credit advices, Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console payout statements denominated in foreign currency) - mandatory to evidence receipt of export consideration from non-resident platform operators.
Non-resident status evidence (W-8BEN-E, Certificate of Residence, or foreign tax identification number of each counterparty platform).
Signed electronic license agreement for multilingual webtoon syndication expressly stating foreign distribution territory and zero-rate GST exclusion.
Valid GST/HST invoice copies with 0% GST notation, itemized by transaction, together with the LP's periodic bank reconcilement.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit flags include continuous zero-rated export claims without documentary proof of non-resident customers, geolocation data showing Canadian downloading, and round-tripping of funds through foreign platforms. Legal exposures: (i) reassessment window extended to unlimited in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default (ITA s.152(4)); ordinary four-year limitation otherwise; (ii) 25% gross negligence penalty on the amount of tax misstated (ITA s.163(2)); (iii) 25% false-statement or omission penalty under ETA s.285.1; (iv) interest at the prescribed rate compounded daily on every GST/HST amount assessed (ETA s.280); (v) reversal of zero-rating, requiring the LP to remit 5% GST on gross export sales retroactively; (vi) joint and several liability of all general and limited partners for the LP's unremitted GST/HST under ETA s.273; (vii) criminal prosecution for wilful evasion (ETA s.327(1), ITA s.239) with fines up to 200% of the tax and imprisonment. Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day inside-benchmark serves as a CRA anti-deferral documentation standard for export revenue substantiation. Export refunds claimed through net zero-rated GST returns are recoverable quarterly, but any tax refund obtained on the basis of false zero-rating claims is clawed back with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canada maintains no dedicated foreign exchange control administration. FX prudential oversight is performed by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), AML/ATF monitoring by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and monetary sovereignty by the Bank of Canada under the Bank of Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible, with Canada in full compliance with IMF Article VIII; there are no current-account or capital-account exchange restrictions and no requirement for central-bank approval of inbound equity or debt contributions. Profit remittance and capital repatriation by a BC limited partnership are unrestricted; however, outbound royalty, interest, management-fee, or similar passive payments to non-residents are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to as low as 0%-15% where the recipient qualifies, e.g., under the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention), and active business income allocated to non-resident partners is reportable on CRA T5013 Partnership Information Returns and taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act. No exchange-control permission, no residence-based ownership approval, and no profit-remittance licence is required for CA_LP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation on a BC limited partnership: there is no mandatory conversion ratio, no maximum foreign-currency retention period, and no requirement to repatriate export or digital-licensing receipts to Canada. Export receipts, webtoon syndication fees, and Apple/Google settlement funds may be retained indefinitely in CAD, USD, or other currencies; however, international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC, and worldwide income remains reportable to the CRA on account of residence regardless of repatriation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional / Medium. Cross-border digital EMIs (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Payoneer, Stripe) are legally viable as supplementary payout and collection rails but cannot serve as the sole treasury custodian for CA_LP. Since the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) came into force in November 2024, payment service providers that perform clearing, settlement, or fund transfers in Canada for end users must be registered or otherwise compliant with the Bank of Canada regime, and entities providing money-services business activities must be registered with FINTRAC. Foreign EMIs operating without Canadian registration or a Canadian payment-service licence may face BN/OSFI enforcement and deposit-taking restrictions; funds held with an EMI are not CDIC-insured and are not protected claims against a Schedule I bank. The recommended treasury design positions the EMI as a settlement adjunct for low-value creator payouts (KRW, PHP, IDR, THB) with daily sweep balances to a regulated Schedule I operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no federal statute mandating physical director appearance; each financial institution applies its own KYC policy under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance. Most Schedule I banks permit account opening through a remote video-identification interview plus digital signature under the BC Electronic Transactions Act, provided at least one authorized signatory (typically an officer of the corporate general partner) presents valid government-issued photo identification. However, a CA_LP with a foreign registered general partner or non-resident authorized signatories will almost certainly trigger enhanced due diligence and a high likelihood of an in-person or designated-person-in-Canada interview before the accounts are activated; incorporation of a BC-resident corporate general partner with a registered records office materially de-risks the onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate general partner and foreign-based authorized signatories with no Canadian nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Limited Partnership from the BC Corporate Registry; executed LP agreement and all amending declarations; certificate of status/good standing of the corporate general partner; notarized directors' resolution authorizing account opening and naming authorised signatories; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration for each material beneficial owner; proof of the BC registered records office (mailing address, registered agent confirmation); and a CRA Business Number confirmation letter for the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value cross-border creator royalty and webtoon syndication flows to Korea, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Vietnam, which may trip transaction-monitoring and structured-transfer alert thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program and Google Play distribution agreements evidencing the digital-content merchant model; specimen content-licensing agreement with sub-publishers; underlying creator contracts and rights schedules; 12-month projected payout ledger with payment reason codes (e.g., 'ROYALTY-WEBTOON'); documented disbursement policy requiring batch settlement through regulated FX counterparties; and a statement confirming FINTRAC large-value transfer reporting obligations are automated in the banking portal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tiered pass-through LP structure with multiple non-resident limited partners, which may be characterised by the bank as beneficial-ownership opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational chart covering the Canadian LP and every upstream corporate and custodial vehicle; KYC/beneficial-ownership schedules for each partner with percentage interests; executed information-sharing and indemnity agreements from limited partners; Canadian tax counsel opinion confirming the arrangement is classified as a partnership (not a foreign corporation) for tax and AML purposes; CRA partnership identification number and T5013 filing plan; and a standing instruction permitting the bank to disclose the full ownership chain to FINTRAC/OSFI on request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant-of-record deposits arriving as commingled subscription revenue, raising questions as to beneficial receipt, chargeback risk, and licence-revenue segregation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreements with Apple and Google; latest monthly settlement statements showing gross billings, platform commissions, and net settlement; end-user terms of service, privacy policy, and content-compliance attestation confirming no regulated or illegal material; internal funds-segregation policy separating IP licence income, subscription collections, and creator-royalty pass-through funds; and a board-approved cash-flow model quantifying expected settlement cycles and balances in the operational account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign partners' capital contributions route by SWIFT MT103 with strict reference to the registered legal name 'CA_LP' to avoid name-mismatch holds; recommended ISO 20022 purpose code 'INVC' (investment capital) or 'BEXP' (business expense) and the narrative 'LP capital contribution - webtoon syndication - [partner name]'. Pre-funding verification comprises (i) the bank's name-screening and OFAC/sanctions cross-check against the LP register, (ii) FINTRAC international-wire reporting for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, (iii) source-of-wealth documentation (capital call notice, LP agreement, partner declaration), and (iv) an Investment Canada Act classification memo confirming that a digital-publishing business below the 2025 WTO investor review threshold (approximately CAD 2.05 billion enterprise value) requires no pre-closing notification filing. No Bank of Canada approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound creator royalties, syndication fees, and content-licence payments settle via (i) SWIFT MT103 for bank-to-bank CAD/USD/EUR remittances with purpose code 'ROYL' or 'LIC' and contract-number references; (ii) MT202 cover payments where the instructing bank utilises a correspondent intermediary; (iii) commercial letters of credit (UCP600) only for bulk content packages in higher-credit-risk jurisdictions where the sub-publisher requires documentary settlement; (iv) Interac e-Transfer or Canadian EFT for domestic creators; and (v) regulated EMI payout rails (Wise, Airwallex, or Payoneer) for low-value KRW, PHP, IDR, and THB disbursements where correspondent SWIFT economics are prohibitive. All outbound wires are subject to the receiving bank's SIP/PEP screening and must evidence the underlying licence agreement in the general ledger record to substantiate the 'low-risk standard' banking tier.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards and vanilla OTC options executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the Canadian FX Master Agreement with a Schedule I bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on creator-market currencies (KRW, PHP, IDR, THB) for hedging local-currency settlement risk, executed via the offshore/restricted-currency desk of a Schedule I bank and subject to OFAC and counterparty-jurisdiction FX-law screening.
Cross-currency swaps in CAD/USD/EUR for long-term licence prepayments and fixed syndication receivables.
Listed CAD/USD futures and options on the Montreal Exchange (TMX) as exchange-traded hedging complements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Consumer Services, Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the limited partnership's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 50 applies; a second consecutive year of non-filing renders the limited partnership subject to administrative dissolution under the BC Limited Partnership Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following a December 31 fiscal period end; otherwise within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under Income Tax Act s.162(9) of CAD 100 per partner per month of delay; gross negligence penalties may apply; unfiled information may block loss claims and prompt audit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for limited partnerships under the BC Limited Partnership Act; audit becomes contractually mandatory if imposed by the partnership agreement, lender, investor, or by CRA for a tax-shelter or investment plan partnership
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE optional for financial statement preparation; tax records must be maintained on an accrual basis in accordance with the Income Tax Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate UBO filing in British Columbia for limited partnerships; the annual report identifies general partners and registered office, while partner changes and ownership shifts are recorded in the internal register of partners and evidenced in the next annual report filing
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General and Limited Partners with contributions and withdrawals
Statutory records containing the partnership agreement, consents, and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500-10,000 per year if a voluntary certified audit is engaged; zero if no audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined federal/BC general corporate income tax rate (15% federal + 12% BC); 11% combined rate for qualifying small business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC). A BC limited partnership is fiscally transparent and does not pay entity-level tax; the rate applies to corporate partners on their allocated income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC small-business deduction (combined federal/BC rate of 11% on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income allocated to a Canadian corporate partner); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits; BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit and Digital Animation Tax Credit (subject to eligibility of webtoon/digital publishing operations and qualifying labour expenditures).
